grades.reason: Covers re-entrant/recursive locks and xv6 forbidding re-acquisition. It doesn't list the necessary conditions for deadlock or explain how lock ordering breaks one.

grades.quote: all code paths that hold multiple locks must acquire locks in the same order.
grades.reason: Gives a concrete deadlock scenario in which two CPUs each hold one lock and wait for the other's. It states the lock-ordering rule that avoids it: every code path acquires locks in the same global order. This shows ordering prevents the circular wait. It never lists the four necessary conditions (mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait) and never names circular wait explicitly.
Covers detecting and recovering from deadlock in database systems through transaction rollback. It doesn't address the necessary conditions or lock ordering.
